external_entities.name: member
external_entities.description: A person who uses the loyalty programme, mobile app, and partner apps.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Members collect points when they shop and spend them on gift cards.

external_entities.name: browser
external_entities.description: A member's browser used to sign in and approve partner-app access.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A member who connects a partner app signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser

external_entities.name: partner app
external_entities.description: A web application operated by another company, such as a meal-planning service that shows a member's points.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers

processes.name: mobile app
processes.description: The mobile application used by members to sign in and call the rewards API.
processes.notes: Nobody wrote down whether the app sends a PKCE challenge.

processes.name: authorization server
processes.description: The server that signs members in, issues authorization codes, refresh tokens, consents, and access tokens.
processes.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow
processes.notes: Nobody decided an idle timeout for the authorization-server sign-in.

processes.name: rewards API
processes.description: The API that reads and writes the points ledger and serves partner and mobile-app requests.
processes.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger

processes.name: support console
processes.description: A web application that closes a member's account.
processes.source_excerpt: The support console is a web app that closes a member's account.

data_stores.name: identity database
data_stores.description: Database containing member identity data, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database

data_stores.name: points ledger
data_stores.description: Ledger containing every member's balance and every points transaction.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the points ledger, which holds every member's balance and every points transaction

data_stores.name: API log store
data_stores.description: Store containing every request received by the rewards API, including headers.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

data_flows.name: use mobile app
data_flows.description: The member uses the mobile app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members use our mobile app.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: The mobile app signs the member in through the authorization server using the authorization code flow.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow
data_flows.notes: Nobody wrote down whether the app sends a PKCE challenge.

data_flows.name: call rewards API
data_flows.description: The mobile app calls the rewards API with an access token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: then calls the rewards API with the access token it gets back

data_flows.name: sign in and consent
data_flows.description: The browser accesses the authorization server sign-in page and submits member consent for the listed scopes.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A member who connects a partner app signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser and approves a consent screen that lists the scopes.

data_flows.name: request tokens
data_flows.description: The partner app sends token requests containing its client secret to the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The partner app sends that secret in the body of its token requests.
data_flows.data_description: client ID, client secret, authorization code, and token request

data_flows.name: return code
data_flows.description: The browser returns an authorization code to the partner app's redirect URI.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The browser then returns to the partner app's redirect URI with an authorization code.

data_flows.name: show points
data_flows.description: The partner app uses the rewards API to show a member's points.
data_flows.source_excerpt: such as a meal-planning service that shows a member's points

data_flows.name: store identity data
data_flows.description: The authorization server stores member identity data, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents in the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database, together with the authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents it issues.
data_flows.data_description: member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents

data_flows.name: delete refresh token
data_flows.description: The mobile app causes a disconnected partner app's refresh token to be deleted from the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members can disconnect a partner app from the settings screen of the mobile app, which deletes that app's refresh token from the identity database.

data_flows.name: read and write ledger
data_flows.description: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger

data_flows.name: write request logs
data_flows.description: The rewards API writes each received request and its headers to the API log store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

data_flows.name: close account
data_flows.description: The support console marks a member's account closed in the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Closing an account marks it closed in the identity database.

trust_boundaries.name: our cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: The organization's cloud-account environment containing the authorization server, rewards API, support console, and data stores.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Everything below runs in our own cloud account

trust_boundaries.name: members' phones
trust_boundaries.description: Phones on which the mobile app runs, outside the organization's cloud account.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: apart from the members' phones and the partner apps

trust_boundaries.name: partner apps' own servers
trust_boundaries.description: Servers operated by other companies for their partner applications.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers

assumptions.assumption: The rewards API is reachable from the internet because it is served on the same public hostname as the support console.
assumptions.basis: The support console and rewards API are served on the same public hostname.

assumptions.assumption: The support console is reachable from the internet because it is served on a public hostname.
assumptions.basis: The support console is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

assumptions.assumption: The identity database contains confidential data because it stores member personal information, password hashes, refresh tokens, authorization codes, and consents.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the store contains member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents.

assumptions.assumption: The points ledger contains confidential data because it stores member balances and points transactions.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the ledger holds every member's balance and every points transaction.

assumptions.assumption: The API log store contains confidential data because request headers may contain bearer credentials and requests may contain member-related data.
assumptions.basis: The source states that every received request, including headers, is stored.
